long: Deletes catalog records without regard to retention periods. It needs full access to every resource.

purge volume all (Onesimus extension) purges every volume of one pool (pool=) or of all pools the console may access (allpools) whose status is one of volstatus= (default Full,Used,Error). It is never interactive: dryrun only shows what would be purged, yes purges.

long: Deletes file records from the catalog regardless of retention periods, for one job (job= or jobid=), a client or a volume; the jobs themselves stay. Like every purge it prints a warning, needs full access to all resources and cannot be undone.
Onesimus deviation: the file records of the latest Full chain of a client and FileSet are skipped, and each purge runs in one transaction whose errors are reported instead of ignored.

examples.explanation: purge the file records of job 599
purge all file records of bareos-fd

long: Deletes whole jobs with all their records regardless of retention periods, for a client, a volume or a pool. jobstatus= limits this to jobs with the given status letters (T, E, f, ...) or names such as error, separated by commas. The Director counts the jobs and asks Purge (yes/no)? unless yes is given. A volume left without jobs becomes Purged.
Onesimus deviation: jobs of the latest Full chain of a client and FileSet are skipped, and each purge runs in one transaction whose errors are reported.

examples.explanation: purge every job on volume Full-0001
purge the failed jobs of pool Incremental

long: Deletes every job on a volume from the catalog regardless of retention; the volume then becomes Purged and can be reused. Several volume= may be given, and each is confirmed on its own unless yes is given. action=truncate or all runs the ActionOnPurge on Purged volumes through the Storage Daemon, with storage=, pool= or allpools, devicetype= and drive=. A volume holding the latest Full chain of a client is never purged (Onesimus).

Onesimus extension: purge volume all purges every volume of pool= or of all permitted pools (allpools) whose status is in volstatus=, by default Full, Used and Error. Purged and Recycle volumes are never selected and Cleaning tapes cannot be purged. It never asks: exactly one of dryrun (preview) and yes is required, and refused volumes are skipped with their reason.

long: Shows and changes the catalog tier of the two-tier console ACLs. The ACL directives of the Console and Profile resources are the outer frame (changed in the editor); the catalog ACL can only restrict further. Effective is what both allow.
set, delete, clear and copy need the CommandACL .acl and configure. Entries are comma separated; commas inside {}, [] or () belong to the entry (regular expressions), a repeated key adds entries.

subs.description: File and catalog entries, effective result
long: Shows per ACL type the file entries (first those of the console, then those of its profiles), the catalog entries and the effective result, plus the load state of the catalog ACL. list is also the default when no subcommand is given. Without console= the own console is shown, or all consoles for a console that may use configure; the ACLs of another console need configure. Catalog entries that only allow what the file ACL forbids are marked as having no effect.

examples.explanation: the ACLs of the own console

long: Replaces the catalog list of the console for every ACL type given. Entries are evaluated like a Bareos list: the first matching entry decides, ! forbids, regular expressions and *all* work as in the file, and a name no entry matches is forbidden. The change takes effect at once. Needs the CommandACL .acl and configure.

The catalog ACL of another console may be changed freely, since it can never go beyond that console's file ACL. On the own console only a narrowing change is allowed: a first list for a type without catalog entries, or a list made from the old one only by inserting ! entries and removing entries without !.

examples.explanation: restrict a console to some clients

long: Removes the given entries from the catalog ACL of the console; a type key without a value removes the whole catalog list of that type, which then no longer restricts. An entry the catalog ACL does not have is an error and nothing changes. Works also for a console that is no longer configured but still has catalog entries. Needs the CommandACL .acl and configure; on the own console only removing entries without ! is allowed.

long: Lists the jobs of the catalog, one row per job. The filters can be combined: job= or jobname=, client=, jobstatus= (letters such as T, E, f or names such as error, comma-separated), jobtype= (letter or exact name such as Backup), joblevel= or level= (F, I, D or Full, Incremental, Differential), volume=, pool=, days= and hours=. last keeps only the latest run per job name, count prints just the number of rows, reverse shows the newest first.

limit= and offset= page through the result. For a console with ACLs the limit is applied before the rows the console may not see are removed, so a limited listing can come out shorter or even empty. An unknown jobtype or level is an error.

Deviation from Bareos: for an unknown job odir reports success, whereas Bareos returns an error. In API mode 2 the result is empty.

long: Prints the grammar of every command the console may run (CommandACL): subcommand words, keywords, key=value arguments, value sources, repeatable keys and exclusive groups. In API mode 2 the reply is the JSON object "grammar" (schema 1), otherwise one usage line per command and subcommand.
oconsole loads it at connect for completion and hints. The Bareos Director does not know the command and answers "is an invalid command"; clients then fall back to .help.
